    Julian the Dragon Tamer¶

    A poor man who lost everything. A prophet who earned a dragon's respect. A legend who became a god.

    Julian was a man from the land that is now Northaxeland (which did not yet exist in his time). His story begins in tragedy and ends in transcendence.

    Early Life¶

    Julian grew up in Shuttil, one of the small kingdoms of the region that would later become Northaxeland. His family was poor — a tiny house, barely enough to survive. When Julian was a child, Shuttil's corrupt guards murdered his family in front of him. They had been blackmailing his parents for unpaid taxes. When the family couldn't pay, the guards killed them and left Julian alive to witness it.

    He fled to the countryside, found work plowing fields. At thirteen, he met Agartha, a woman who would change his life. They married two years later. He trained in martial arts obsessively. They eventually moved out of Shuttil and settled near the capital of Baoth, where Julian started a beer delivery business. At nineteen, he had two children.

    The Breaking¶

    An aristocrat from Baoth — possessed by the Shadows, acting strange and predatory — found Julian's wife beautiful. After she refused his advances, he murdered her and both of Julian's children in cold blood.

    When Julian discovered what had happened, he broke. He left his house without a destination.

    The Lyrical Forest¶

    Wandering, Julian passed through the Lyrical Forest. There he fell down a slope — falling for what felt like hours. At the bottom, he found a tree that began to speak. The tree told him: go to Dragonreach. You may find your family again.

    Believing himself insane, Julian went.

    The Journey¶

    The journey from the Lyrical Forest to Dragonreach took two months. On the way, Julian encountered three adventurers:

    • Diana — a human woman
    • Plenio — an elf
    • Korvald — a kobold

    They joked about his situation and didn't believe him at first. But they kept following — curious to see what would become of him. At the entrance to Dragonreach, they asked: "You really want to do this?" Julian said yes and moved forward.

    After a pause, they followed. Plenio spoke for all three: "Either we die in glory or live to see another day under honor."

    The Unjust Duel¶

    They climbed Dragonreach, passing through the ruins of the old dragon kings. Fallen dragons circled them — watching, but not attacking. Something was different.

    Fireborn — father of Goldenborn, former dragon king of Klobiendar, now a Fallen Dragon — appeared before them. He challenged Julian to what he called "An unjust duel."

    Julian accepted.

    The fight lasted ten hours. Julian lost an arm. Most of his teeth. His face was disfigured beyond recognition. And he kept fighting — until he reached one centimeter from Fireborn's core of life.

    Fireborn immediately acknowledged him as the prophet.

    Fireborn summoned Plenio, Diana, and Korvald from their hiding place and demanded they swear loyalty to Julian or die. They swore.

    Fireborn spilled the black agent onto Julian's body. Julian was consumed and restored — his limbs regrown, his appearance healed. Julian begged for his family's return. Fireborn answered: "You will meet them once the waters come to die, the airs start to cool down, and the monsters from the depths come back" — an allegory for post-Divergence that no one at the time could understand.

    Julian accepted the words as if his family could never return.

    Fireborn gave him the Sword of Xi and told him the truth: an evil called the Hybrians had come to Ge'or, sent to destroy all families. Julian's family was their victim.

    The March on Baoth¶

    Julian left Dragonreach and marched toward Baoth, leaving a trail of destruction. Plenio, Diana, and Korvald instigated the population to rise against Baoth and Dragon King Goldenborn.

    In the capital, Julian met Goldenborn himself. Goldenborn was not yet possessed by the Shadows, but manipulated — flattered, isolated, kept ignorant of what was happening in his kingdom. He asked Julian: "Why are you doing this to our kingdom, which has done nothing to deserve it?"

    A Shadow-controlled army surrounded Julian. He tried to tell Goldenborn the truth. Goldenborn disregarded everything.

    After a fight, Julian was injured but escaped.

    The Grave¶

    Julian went to the grave of his wife, his daughter, and his son. He opened it with his own hands. He touched their bodies.

    Nothing happened — or so he thought.

    Then he heard their voices. All three of them, telling him to rest.

    Julian died on the spot. Disheartened. Complete.

    His body and the skeletons of his family immediately disintegrated into the black agent. Amid the chaos, Fireborn flew above Baoth and consumed Julian's disintegrating corpse. He returned to Dragonreach.

    In that moment, Julian incarnated into Fireborn. And Julian learned: to get his family back, he must wait for two prophets who are coming in the future. He must test them. He must prove them.

    Legacy¶

    The Alegoria Religion¶

    The Axels — the human people of what became Northaxeland — created a new religion under the legendary figure of Julian, believing he became one with their god. This religion is called Alegoria.

    The Church of Alegoria controls most of northern Erisdar. It is also the faith of the Ameboria region inside Kent — which, as of 597 AGD, is in civil war trying to separate from Kent. The rest of Kent follows the Erisian faith and hates the Alegorians. Venkradian Republic and Loren are also majority Alegorian.

    The Sword of Xi¶

    The Sword of Xi fell during the chaos in Baoth. Anyone who tried to hold it immediately died. The Axels built a monument around it. Those ruins still stand in the Ruins of Baoth, and the sword remains in the ground at that exact location.

    The Three Companions¶

    Plenio, Diana, and Korvald continued guerrilla warfare against Baoth's influence. They eventually settled in the Northaxeland region, where the population was most in favor of their cause. Entire cities raised armies. Some declared independence from Baoth. Shuttil — Julian's birthplace, now allied to Baoth — was the first victim of this league. The Axels invaded and destroyed it.

    Plenio, Diana, and Korvald became loyal servants of the Axel people, guiding them into the future.
